title.narrative: Promoting Equal Rights for Women and Girls with Disabilities (PERD Project)

description.narrative: 1.To contribute towards the protection of the fundamental human rights particularly sexual and gender-based violence against women and girls with disabilities in Ghana by the end of August 2024.2.To empower Women and Girls with Disabilities to pursue employment opportunities by the end of August 2024.3.To advocate for the development and implementation of the inclusive equitable employment policies for WGDs in public and private sectors institutions in Ghana by the end of August 2024.

Based on analysis of their comparable advantages in women and girls’ human rights related interests, organizational competence, values, geographical locations and areas of operation the Planned Parenthood Association of Ghana (PPAG), Women in Need (WIN) and Africa Centre for Human Rights and Sustainable Development (AfCHuRSD) are collaborating to implement the PERD Project. The PERD Project is a joint project implemented by women-led organizations (PPAG, AfCHuRSD and WIN) with funding from the Dutch Embassy in Ghana. The interventions is tailored at promoting the fundamental human rights of Women and Girls with Disability (WGDs) particularly the rights to employment and the protection from Sexual Gender Based Violence (SGBV) in Ghana. The project will be collaborating with the Ghana Federation of Disability Organisations (GFD), Ghana Council of Disability and other relevant stakeholders. The team understands the necessity of creating the right ambience for the effective implementation of various interventions to achieve equal economic rights of WGDs.

Primary Target Group: Women and Girls with DisabilitySecondary Target : Government and Private institution/organizationGovernment : Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection, Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations ,Social Welfare, Department of Children, Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies, Department of Gender and Domestic Violence Secretariat, Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ), Legal Aid and Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU). Private institution/organization : Ghana Federation of Disability and the National Council of Disability

title.narrative: Final PERD project Narrative report for Year One( September 2021 to August 2022)
1.6 Engagements with selected DCEs on the implementation of their 3% of the DACF towards improving the sustainable economic livelihoods of WGDs

description.narrative: As per the District Assembly Common Fund (DACF), a 3% of the fund is dedicated to PWDs but however, there is no clear structure on its disbursement and the sustainable economic livelihoods of WGDs. This activity intends to engage the District Assembly to inquire about the status of the fund and how it is being managed

title.narrative: Number of DCEs engaged on the implementation of the 3% of the DACF

comment.narrative: A total of seven (7) DCEs were engaged across the project implementation on the implementation of their 3% of the District Assembly Common Fund (DACF), Specifically, three (3) in the Northern zone (,Nadowli-Kaleo District,Jirapa and Sagnarigu Municipal , one (1) in the Middle( Kwabre East Municipal) and three (3) in the Southern zone ( Mfantseman Municipal, Gomoa West and Ajumako/Enyan/Essiam Districts.. General feedback from DCEs engaged across the implementing sites was the untimely disbursement of funds to the districts due to delays from the head office in Accra. However once received, funds are disbursed to selected beneficiaries through a rigorous process and lodged directly into their account for easy accessibility. The insufficiency of the funds coupled with the large number of applicants was one profound challenges raised by the DCEs across the districts. The assembly as a result has to prioritize beneficiaries in terms of their needs. For example, in the northern zone they may prioritize education when they know schools are reopening and students (WGDs) require funds to pay their fees. They may also prioritize applicants in farming, especially during the rainy season when they need seeds, fertilizers, their fields to be ploughed, etc. “Based on past experiences where beneficiaries failed to invest the funds they accessed in their businesses, we now purchase whatever items are needed and help set up the business for them,”- DCE for Nadowli. With this strategy, most of the PWDs in the district that accessed the fund are doing well in their businesses.Another challenge the project addressed through the engagements with the DCEs was to orient the fund management committee members and representatives of the disability community on the new 3% District Assembly Common Fund disbursement guidelines. Participants in these meetings discussed how to effectively disburse the Fund to PWDs to maximize its impact, and shared experiences and brought up some challenges and how to address them. Follow-up actions included, GFD pledging to also orient their members on the new guidelines specifically on how to access the fund. Which is intended to provide clarity on the fund allocation and disbursement processes and empower WGDs in the implementing sites to demand accountability. The engagement with the MCEs/DCE and officers in charge at the Department of Social Welfare in the Municipal and district assemblies in the implementing sites fostered a good working relationship and enabled the project team to collaborate with them to educate project beneficiaries on the processes involved in accessing the 3% DACF.

For instance, in the southern zone, selected trained champions together with the Central Regional GFD president have visited Darling FM in Cape Coast. They had discussions on rights, especially the rights of WGDs, the Affirmative Action Bill, the Employment Equity Policy, and psychological stress among people with disabilities. During the discussion, they admonished the public not to discriminate against persons with disabilities, especially women and girls. Also, in the Northern zone, a radio program was organized at Radio Progress in WA. Selected WGD champions, the Chairman of the Wa Municipal Blind Association, and the former Regional Representative of the GFD in the Upper West Region during the radio discussion highlighted the processes involved in accessing the 3% DACF for persons with disabilities and addressing discrimination and stigma against of persons with disabilities, especially women and girls. title.narrative: 1.5. Support activities of the Affirmative Action Collation towards the passing of the AA-Bill (media engagement, awareness creation…)

description.narrative: Partnering and supporting the Affirmative Action Coalition to conduct media advocacy towards the passage of the Affirmative Action Bill

title.narrative: Number of times the PERD project support AAB coalition toward the passage of the bill

comment.narrative: In Year two, one collaboration was made by the project with Affirmative Action Coalition to organize an inter-partner dialogue dubbed” Uniting for Action to End Sexual and Gender-Based Violence Against Women and Girls with Disability to push for the passage of the Affirmative Action Bill into law”. The forum was also in commemoration of 2022 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-based Violence which was held at the Netherlands embassy in Accra. Thirty (30) individuals including members and stakeholders participated in the activity. The Ambassador of the Netherlands Embassy, H.E Jeroen Verheul, made a cameo appearance and shared that “Efforts have been put in place for years yet the Bill has not been passed. So, we need to look at what can be done differently to ensure the Bill is passed into law”. Madam Sheila Minka-Premo, the convener of the Affirmative Action Bill (AABill) Coalition, mentioned that the AABill also known as the Gender Equality Bill, seeks to provide an accountability framework for measuring gender equality and empowerment as well as increase participation of women in leadership. She highlighted the fact that in 2016, the bill was laid in parliament. To date, the bill has not yet been passed into law. The following strategies were adopted by participants during the forum: engaging young people with more vibrancy, passion, and knowledge of social media to advocate for the Bill, and to kick-start the circulation of campaign messages on the AABill through print and electronic media aimed to sensitize the public and whip their interest for support. “The strategies developed during the group discussions would be put together to reinforce the already existing ones and used for the advocacy,” Madam Sheila said. The forum's achievement was the development of strategies for advocacy work on the AABill, coupled with the coalition's willingness to collaborate continuously on this campaign, which was a success. In Year Three, the steering committee of the Affirmative Action Bill Coalition and some key members including representatives from the PERD consortium paid a courtesy call on the newly appointed Minister of Gender, Children, and Social Protection, Hon. Darkoa Newman. The delegation led by the AABill Convener, Mrs Sheila Minkah-Premo Esq sought an update from the Ministry on the progress of the Bill given Parliament’s resumption from recess in the week ahead. The Honourable Minister assured the delegation that she was in contact with key members of the Parliamentary Committee on Gender and Children and assured the delegation that the AA Bill would surely be passed during this session. She thanked the Coalition for its technical support and advocacy over the years and encouraged it to intensify its media advocacy.In July 2024, The PERD project collaborated with the Coalition when the AABILL was relayed in parliament and supported the coalition during the windowing (brief meetings with at least five parliamentarians before sitting began) in parliament from Monday 22nd July 2024 till the bill was passed. The PERD project again collaborated with the coalition to mobilize women to parliament to give support to the Hon Minister which was duly acknowledged by the Rt. Hon Speaker. The AABill was finally passed into Law on 30th July 2024 after a series of amendments. Currently called the Affirmative Action Gender Equity Act. Pending the president’s accent.The PERD consortium financially supported the AABill Coalition two times to carry out key activities that led to the enactment of the Bill.

In year two, At the district level, 9 engagements were made with the GFD to support project implementation. 6 of these engagements were made at the district level during the field implementation. The district-level engagements were targeted toward creating awareness and educating WGDs on how to access the DACF.However, at the national level, the GFD was engaged in 3 important meetings about getting the Equitable Employment Policy. (1) The GFD was involved in a meeting with the PERD Consortium, MELR, and NCPD at the national level, the outcome of the meeting was to propose a merger of the 2 versions proposed by GFD and NCPD into a consolidated draft Equitable Employment policy which was submitted to MELR and reviewed by stakeholders in a stakeholder consultative meeting. (2) Representatives of the GFD were part of a Technical Working Group (TWG) meeting on Employment Equity Policy. The objective of the meeting is to review the draft Employment Equity Policy and make it one document for consideration for the stakeholders’ meeting. The outcome of the meeting was to engage a consultant to assist in shaping the policy per the national guidelines to make it worthy to be submitted to the Cabinet for approval.(3) Finally the GFD was involved in stakeholder meetings with other duty bearers to deliberate on the draft policy presented by the technical working group. Some representatives of the various Ministries, Departments, Agencies, Civil Society Organizations, Ghana Federation of Disability Organizations (GFD), National Council on Persons with Disability (NCPD), PERD Project, PPAG, AfCHuRSD, and WIN) were present to share their comments and input on the PolicyIn year 3, 2 engagements were made with the GFD. The engagements led to the draft of the final version of the Equitable Employment policy. In total, the PERD project collaborated with the GFD in 14 different engagements at the National and district levels.
